user_prompt: As of Alphabet Inc.'s FY2025 balance sheet, do total liabilities stay within total assets according to the record's own reported figures (i.e., positive reported net worth)?
scope: The single embedded REAL SEC XBRL record GOOGL-BS-FY2025 (top-level records.GOOGL-BS-FY2025 of this instance file), fetched verbatim via bench/fetch_edgar.py from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0001652044.json (PROVENANCE in artifacts/fin-googl/PROVENANCE; restructured from SEC's own list-of-entries shape into flat named keys, see module docstring), read exclusively via inspect_record(record_id='GOOGL-BS-FY2025', field_path=...): entityName (filer identity), assets.val/fy/fp/form/concept and liabilities.val/fy/fp/form/concept (the SAME period-end, 2025-12-31, both Form 10-K; 'val' is the literal leaf field name in BOTH -- field_path='assets.val' reads total Assets, field_path='liabilities.val' reads total Liabilities). The verdict is scoped to whether the record's OWN two balance-sheet figures show Liabilities at or below Assets as of that ONE period-end -- not to any market-value or off-balance-sheet consideration; no external market-data lookup or human/LLM judgment is used or available. GROWTH/ARITHMETIC-CLAIM DESIGN NOTE (mirrors the YoY-growth instances in this domain): the closed predicate grammar only compares one field against a fixed constant, so the field-vs-field 'Liabilities <= Assets' comparison is kept decidable by setting atom E5's numeric_le threshold to Assets' own real value (established exactly by atom E3); E5 then mechanically evaluates the solvency comparison via the ordinary numeric_le predicate over the actual field the tool reads.

claims.text: The record's filer identity and the existence of a reported total-Assets figure as of FY2025 period-end are located in the supplied record.
The identifying/existence facts are established (C1) and the record's total Assets figure is confirmed to equal exactly $595,281,000,000.

Under the supplied record, total Assets ($595,281,000,000) and total Liabilities ($180,016,000,000) as of the SAME FY2025 period-end are both established from the record's own balance-sheet entries, and Liabilities do not exceed Assets: the record supports a positive-reported-net-worth verdict as of that period-end.

atoms.proposition: The record's filer identity is read via inspect_record(field_path='entityName') and found present.
The record's total Assets figure as of FY2025 period-end is read via inspect_record(field_path='assets.val') and found present.
The same Assets figure is read again and found to equal exactly $595,281,000,000.

The record's total Liabilities figure as of the SAME period-end (a DISJOINT top-level field from E2/E3's Assets entry) is read via inspect_record(field_path='liabilities.val') and found to equal exactly $180,016,000,000.

The Liabilities figure is read a second time and evaluated against the Assets figure's own reported value ($595,281,000,000, established by E3) as the ceiling: found Liabilities does NOT exceed Assets -- the record's own balance-sheet solvency check, decided mechanically by the closed grammar's numeric_le predicate over the actual field the tool reads at run time.
Non-route background: the filing form type backing the Assets figure is read and found to be '10-K' -- not required for, and not evidence toward, the solvency claim.
